note: Pattern rules for machines whose reported identifiers do not equal a pack folder name. Seeded from the SCCM driver-apply step conditions, which are the production-proven matching logic. Evaluated IN ORDER, first match wins, AFTER the SystemSKU index and BEFORE the model-name and baseboard fallbacks. 'on' selects the WMI property: model = Win32_ComputerSystem.Model, baseboard = Win32_BaseBoard.Product. 'match' is a PowerShell -like pattern (* and ? are wildcards; + is literal).

rules.why: SCCM: Win32_BaseBoard WHERE Product LIKE '%CF33-2%'. Toughbooks report nothing useful in ComputerSystem.Model, and the Product string carries affixes, so an exact folder match never fires.
SCCM: Product='FZ55-1' - exact, unlike its siblings
MUST precede the general Pro 10 rule below, or the 5G variant resolves to the non-5G pack
SCCM: Model LIKE 'Surface Pro 7+'. This pack can NEVER resolve by name: the folder-name transform turns '+' into '_', so Surface_Pro_7+ is unreachable without a rule. Must precede the Pro 7 rule.
SCCM: Model LIKE 'Surface Pro 7' - exact, so it does not also catch the 7+
SCCM: Model LIKE '%Surface Laptop 7 for Business'

Replaces an alias junction. This exact string is reported by a real fleet device (1 unit); Dell's catalog calls the platform brand 'Dell Pro Max Laptops', systemID 0DB4. SKU 0DB4 resolves it at stage 1, so this rule only fires when SystemSKU is not reported - which is exactly what the junction used to cover, for 8.44 GiB per stick.
Replaces an alias junction. Word-order variant of the folder name; systemID 0A3C. SKU 0A3C resolves it at stage 1, so this rule only covers the SKU-less case - 5.45 GiB per stick as a junction.
